title: Currying, partial application, and compose
hook: Currying turns f(a,b,c) into f(a)(b)(c) for reusable specialized functions. compose chains unary transforms — pipe is compose reversed. Common in FP libraries and React reselect selectors.

blocks.text: **Currying** transforms a multi-argument function into nested unary functions returning functions until all args collected. **Partial application** fixes some args with bind or wrapper — not always unary chain. **compose(f, g)(x)** equals **f(g(x))** — right-to-left. **pipe** is left-to-right for readability. JavaScript functions are **variadic** — manual curry helpers common; not language-native like Haskell.

entries.plainDefinition: Transform fn(a,b) into fn(a)(b) — each call takes one argument.
entries.example: const add = a => b => a + b; add(2)(3);

entries.plainDefinition: Fix subset of arguments, return function needing rest.
Single parameter — compose chains typically unary.

blocks.text: **Reselect** memoized selectors compose pure functions. Middleware patterns curry `(store) => (next) => (action) =>`. Configurable validators: `const isMin = min => value => value >= min`. C# has no native curry — **Func** currying manual; **method chaining** on builders is different pattern. Interviews: implement curry and compose.

blocks.title: Interview trap: curry vs partial
blocks.body: Curry: one arg per call until arity satisfied. Partial: fix some args in one shot. bind(null, 1) is partial, not necessarily curried unary chain.

snippet.explanation: fn.length excludes rest parameters — curry helpers break on ...rest unless arity provided.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Currying functions with rest/default params using fn.length. compose order reversed vs pipe. Over-currying simple two-arg functions hurting readability. Losing this binding with unbound composed methods.

blocks.text: Use curry for **configuration reuse** (API clients, validators), not every function. **Memoize** composed selectors (reselect). TypeScript: use overloads or tuple typing for advanced curry. Know Ramda **pipe** vs **compose** naming. In interviews write 10-line curry and compose without libraries.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot implement compose. Confusing curry with partial application. Unaware fn.length pitfall with rest parameters.

interviewTakeaways: Curry: nested unary functions until arity met; partial fixes args upfront.
compose(f,g)(x) = f(g(x)); pipe is reverse order.
fn.length breaks with rest/default parameters — specify arity manually.
60s: Curry for reusable specialized functions. compose reduceRight. bind for partial. C# Func nesting manual. Middleware currying pattern.
Follow-up: implement pipe and curry with explicit arity parameter.
commonPitfalls: Using fn.length for variadic functions in curry helper.
Reversing compose vs pipe order incorrectly.
Strong answer: implement curry+compose, contrast partial bind, middleware example, C# Func parallel.
